newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM sees no quick budget change after flood.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM sees no quick budget change after flood.

text.p: Poland's prime minister decided on Friday not to seek an immediate 1997 budget change to create more funds for a flood relief programme, a government spokeswoman said.

"We have come to a conclusion that problems can be solved without amending the budget at the moment," Aleksandra Jakubowska told Reuters. By law, parliament can amend the budget only at the government's request.

She said the government could reconsider changing the budget in several weeks after experts outline necessary aid schemes and detail damages from the six-day flood that has killed 23 people and put some 3,500 square km under water.
But Jakubowska said the 500 million zlotys ($151.3 million) that the government had carved out from various budget reserves to help flood victims was enough for now.
"The review of the situation, experts say, can be done within four weeks after water subsides, possibly in mid-July, and the government will then ponder if the allocated money is enough," she said.

Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz decided to open state food reserves, which include canned meat, butter, lard, drugs and toilet articles, she said. Southern province governors affected by the flood can apply for them.
Jakubowska said Poland did not need extra food imports.
